rv.q: On the contrary, they crackle quite delightfully as Hallahan's Jake exposes his neuroses along with his romantic potential, and Escalante's empathetic Ros (get the reference?) strives for happiness in one recognizable costume after another.
All The World is a charming love letter to theater, acting, and life, both onstage and off.
Radiant, captivating, and moving, All the World showcases theater at its finest.
Thebus, who has directed Gunderson's work before in her impressive CV, is absolutely a perfect choice for this one.
Together with all the artists involved, they have conjured a real holiday treat at Northlight with simple tools— the English language, artistic excellence and storytelling par excellence.
Ros and Jake magical and amusing chemistry on stage is engaging, making you truly root for a successful offstage relationship in this romantic comedy-drama.
Escalante is particularly stunning in her commitment to her theatrical career.

Escalante and Hallahan’s chemistry is palpable here, and Thebus knows how to situate us in this backstage world that, like green rooms everywhere, hums with anticipation of what’s next—and memories of the performances that disappear so quickly into the theatrical ether.
Director Jessica Thebus led her performers with a light touch, allowing room for flirtation, seduction, separation and a fitting end.
This is a play that works well with Northlight and their new venue.

cn.t: Critics praise *All the World* as a charming, romantic delight. Gunderson's witty backstage love story, smoothly directed by Jessica Thebus, earns strong acclaim for its warmth, theatrical insight, and irresistible rom-com spirit.
